@{63b9d9d37085c032e82e9706|full_name} IP bans are easy to get around. You can get a new IP even without a VPN pretty quickly depending on your ISP. Sometimes just restarting your PC and router can grab you a new one.

Hardware ban might work? I'm not sure how that's done though.

I've seen a reasonably high rate of action taken against people I report. The only two reasons I have seen that a report has been ignored are;

1) Not enough evidence - I.e. video footage wasn't clear on context.

2) The evidence was posted elsewhere first.

VRChat has a policy where they won't take action against evidence uploaded to another platform. I don't know why but I assume because of the possibility of it being edited or taken out of context (though whose to say a directly uploaded video isn't edited).

In terms of it being reported to authorities, their policy says they will share the info with authorities though they aren't going to tell the person reporting because that could compromise an investigation. Whether they do or not idk.

What I can say is that online crimes take years to be actioned against. I have friends who were groomed and have reported directly to authorities. One got a groomer 19 years prison time, after about 1.5 years investigation. Another it's been nearly 2 years since their technology has been returned for evidence collection and no word since - besides finding out a number of victims were involved: so that investigation is likely still going.

I guess this can be marked as "Complete" now? VRChat published a blog post: [Update: Age Assurance, Content Gating, and Safety Improvements in VRChat](https://hello.vrchat.com/blog/june-2026-safety-update)
